subject: sociology
title: Society as a Body
welcome_lead: Meet the functionalists who pictured society as a living organism — every institution an organ doing its job.
meta_desc: GCSE Sociology adventure on functionalism: the organic analogy, Durkheim and value consensus.
final_note: You now know why functionalists call society an organism and what 'consensus' really means.

walkthroughs.body_html: Durkheim said institutions are like organs. Family is the heart that socialises children; school is the brain that trains them; the economy is the muscles. Each must do its job for the whole to survive.
Durkheim said early small societies had mechanical solidarity — people were similar and felt close. Modern societies have organic solidarity based on people doing different but interdependent jobs.
Functionalists argue society needs value consensus: agreement that hard work pays, honesty matters, families care for children. Without this agreement, society breaks down into anomie.
